questions.q: What is the key difference between an infrastructure rollback and a model rollback?
options: There is no real difference, they are the same operation
Infrastructure rollback reverts the serving deployment itself; model rollback points the serving layer back at a previous model version, often without touching infrastructure
Model rollback only works in SageMaker
Infrastructure rollback is always faster than model rollback
questions.explain: Infrastructure rollback undoes a bad deploy (e.g. a bad config), while model rollback is typically a pointer change (an alias) back to a previous model version.

questions.q: Why is moving a registry alias back to a previous version often the fastest rollback path?
options: It requires rebuilding the container image
It's a pointer change that a serving job picks up on its next alias resolution, with no redeploy or rebuild required
It automatically restarts every pod in the cluster
It deletes the bad model version permanently
questions.explain: Alias-based rollback avoids any rebuild or redeploy — it just repoints which version the alias resolves to, taking effect almost immediately.

questions.q: What does `kubectl rollout undo` actually do?
options: It deletes the current Deployment permanently
It reverts a Deployment to the previous ReplicaSet that Kubernetes keeps in its revision history by default
It rolls back a model registry alias
It pauses all traffic to the cluster
questions.explain: Kubernetes retains prior ReplicaSets, and rollout undo reverts the Deployment to the previous one — the right tool for a bad deployment config, not necessarily a bad model.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what kind of signal should trigger an automatic rollback rather than routing to a human decision?
options: Any single data point that looks slightly off
A sustained threshold breach in error rate/latency, or a canary's predictions sharply diverging from the incumbent
A model that is one day old
Any deployment made outside business hours
questions.explain: Clear, sustained metric breaches or sharp prediction divergence are unambiguous enough to automate; borderline or slow-moving signals should go to a human instead.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say rollback speed is 'decided earlier, at packaging and registry time'?
options: Because rollback speed is random and cannot be influenced
Because design choices like alias-based registries and traffic-split routing are what make 'go back' a pointer change instead of a full rebuild
Because packaging has no relationship to rollback
Because only SageMaker supports fast rollback
questions.explain: A team that only ever replaces the production model in place has no fast rollback path; alias and traffic-split patterns set up earlier are what make fast rollback possible later.
